claims.claim_paraphrase: Applying a model calibrated for an earlier mid-early silage maize hybrid to a newer hybrid caused systematic growth and yield discrepancies; hybrid-specific physiological parameter adjustments improved model performance.
claims.evidence_locator: Abstract, p.1; Discussion: hybrid-specific dry matter production and partitioning; Results: Yield prediction performance in a large-scale evaluation

source_context.region: Germany, northern to central field experiments
source_context.cultivar: KWS Ronaldinio and KWS Gunnario; two mid-early hybrids
source_context.measurement: process model evaluated with field biomass and final silage yield; not a direct cultivar suitability test
source_context.methods: field trials and process-based model; high N treatments intended to exclude N stress

limitations: No general maize cultivar ranking or target yield
No Dutch parcel or 2027 field validation
No universal temperature threshold, root depth or MCFT parameter transfer

claims.claim_paraphrase: The German large-scale evaluation included 287 site-year observations; final-yield relative RMSE was 0.16 for the older hybrid and 0.21 for the newer hybrid after hybrid-specific parameterization. Drought and nitrogen stress responses require refinement.
claims.evidence_locator: Abstract p.1; Material and methods: Data sets; Results: Yield prediction performance in a large-scale evaluation, Figure 4; Discussion

source_context.years: national evaluation 2006–2021 as reported in Data sets
source_context.measurement: relative root mean square error of final silage yield model predictions; not MAPE or observation error
source_context.methods: national hybrid trials; coarser soil/weather inputs

limitations: Not directly comparable with soybean MAPE
No field-level uncertainty calibration or 2027 yield
No claim about N or drought treatment efficacy

claims.claim_paraphrase: The regional analysis identifies cool northern conditions and shorter seasons as limitations; cultivar cold adaptation and maturity matter.
claims.evidence_locator: Abstract; crop performance discussion surrounding Figure 2, clusters B/C; Methods: Crop modelling and simulations

source_context.cultivars: model maturity groups 0000–III, not a named field cultivar
source_context.years: 1999–2018 historical weather; separate field trial comparison includes Netherlands
source_context.measurement: simulation at 0.5-degree grid with phenology/growth models; maturity at R7; rainfed scenarios; no calibration to European trials

limitations: No selected 2027 cultivar or local weather/soil inputs
Cannot identify the PDOK polygon's cluster by assumption
No cross-crop rank or prescribed action

claims.claim_paraphrase: Out-of-sample rainfed trial comparison had 84 observations and 36% mean absolute percentage error; results are evidence of regional plausibility rather than exact parcel yield.
claims.evidence_locator: Methods: Simulation data processing, PDF page 10 (one-based), Supplementary Fig. 1

source_context.region: Belgium, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Spain, UK
source_context.measurement: comparison of simulated rainfed yield potential to observed maturity-group mean yields

limitations: Do not treat simulation output as observations
No target yield, maturity date or ranking inferred
